clue.text: Master responsible for taking care of me

parts.note: to be over something is to be in charge of it
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in charge who looks after the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only links the pieces; 'care of' is the c/o seen on envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a difficulty is to conquer or prevail over it.

clue.text: Heavy metal, maybe so retrograde?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Heavy metal, maybe so retrograde? (6)': no reversal of these words gives OSMIUM (it needs MUIMSO read backwards); likely an OCR garble of the printed clue, and no scan or search gives the original.

clue.text: Ten unusual diamonds are alluring

definitions.note: plural verb phrase, matching the plural verb form of the answer with diamonds as subject

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of ten appear in an odd new order

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Ten remarkable diamonds are tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TEN into ENT; ICE is underworld slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or tempt someone is to be alluring to them.

clue.text: Film star had a meal, getting act together

parts.note: Gary Cooper, Hollywood film star
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A movie actor dined and then sorted himself out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting act together' looks like the idiom for sorting oneself out, but the definition is literal: acting jointly.
explanation.definitionFit: Working jointly with others is acting in partnership.

clue.text: Money tinkles when circulating in town

indicators.note: circulating money moves round, so the letters of money tinkles are moved about

explanation.surface: Cash jingles as it passes from hand to hand in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: MILTON KEYNES is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England. 'when circulating' rearranges MONEY TINKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Keynes is an English new town, an example of the definition.

clue.text: A biro's taken out to produce curve on map

indicators.note: letters taken out and jumbled, so a biro's is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out a ballpoint pen to draw a line on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' rearranges A BIRO'S, the 's counting as a letter here. A biro is a British ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are lines on a weather chart joining points of equal pressure.

clue.text: Lift what's been an ailing British industry, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is said aloud and a sound-alike is entered

parts.words: what's been an ailing British industry
parts.note: the British steel industry declined sharply in the late twentieth century

explanation.surface: A comment on lifting things and a struggling British manufacturing sector.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is slang for pinching or stealing it.

clue.text: Unconventional person such as Wenceslas?

definitions.meaning: an artistic free spirit living outside social norms
Good King Wenceslas was Duke of Bohemia, so a native of that land

explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian is an arty nonconformist, and also a native of Bohemia, Wenceslas's realm.

clue.text: Reactionary types showing signs of being hot under the collar?

definitions.meaning: a derogatory name for conservative rural Americans

definitions.text: showing signs of being hot under the collar?
definitions.meaning: literally, people whose necks are flushed, as when angry

explanation.definitionFit: The term means ultra-conservative country folk, and literally describes people with flushed, sunburnt necks.

clue.text: Dull leader of republic, just staid and podgy?

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, without shine

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of republic

parts.note: only means just, merely

explanation.surface: A drab head of state is merely sedate and plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' gives R, the first letter of 'republic'; MAT is a variant spelling of matt.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle-aged woman of sedate manner and stout figure is described this way.

clue.text: Technique gone through at front of house to get door opening

indicators.note: at front of places the first piece before the next one

parts.note: to have met something is to have experienced or gone through it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of door

explanation.surface: A method of getting the front door open after passing through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front of' sets the first piece before the second; 'opening' takes the first letter of 'door'. Ho. is the address abbreviation for house.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a systematic way or procedure for doing something.

clue.text: Most valuable assistant about whom there's nothing sinister?

definitions.meaning: one's chief and most trusted helper
sinister is Latin for left, so someone with nothing left about him is all right side

explanation.definitionFit: A chief aide is so called, and literally the phrase means a man on the right, not the sinister left.

clue.text: Relation, about fifty, taken in by a French female

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the following piece

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a
c, short for circa, means about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A relative around fifty is housed by a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' places C (circa) and L (fifty) inside UNE, French for 'a' with a feminine noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, a parent's brother.

clue.text: Flag round gun a military medal incorporated

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: incorporated means taken inside the gun word

parts.note: a rifle is a gun
MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal, a British award

explanation.surface: A banner draped around a firearm with a decoration attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporated' puts the medal inside the gun. The oriflamme was the sacred red banner of the French kings; MM is a British gallantry award.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the royal battle standard of medieval France.

clue.text: Be faced with a terminally overboard situation?

definitions.text: Be faced with a terminally overboard situation?

parts.words: Be faced with a terminally overboard situation?
parts.note: the pirates' punishment of making a captive step off a board over the sea, ending his life

explanation.definitionFit: Pirates allegedly forced victims to step off a plank into the sea, a fatal fall overboard.

clue.text: Beneath the vain display there lurks a sullen mistress

indicators.note: in a down entry, beneath places the later pieces under the first

parts.note: pomp is ostentatious show
dour means sullen, gloomy

explanation.surface: Behind showy pageantry hides a sulky lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beneath' sets A DOUR under POMP in this down entry. Madame de Pompadour was the mistress of Louis XV.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame de Pompadour was the celebrated royal favourite of Louis XV of France.

clue.text: Where you may, find tea, that's virtually certain

definitions.meaning: literally, tea is often sold inside little bags
idiom for something as good as secured

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means assured of success, and tea leaves come packed inside sachets.

clue.text: Country long restricted by revolutionary voices

indicators.note: restricted by means held inside the next piece
revolutionary means the word for voices turns round and is read backwards

parts.note: airs are tunes, melodies for the voice
lank describes long, limp hair

explanation.surface: A nation is constrained by rebel voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the voices word round, giving SRIA, and 'restricted by' puts the long word inside it. Airs are songs, hence voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation south of India, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Night lines of help to those with baby-sitting problems?

definitions.text: Night lines of help to those with baby-sitting problems?

parts.words: Night lines of help to those with baby-sitting problems?
parts.note: verses sung or recited at bedtime to settle a fretful infant

explanation.definitionFit: Short traditional verses for children are recited to soothe little ones at bedtime.

clue.text: Crooner is without sex appeal? That's cruel

indicators.note: without means outside, so the crooner surrounds the next piece

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A ballad singer lacks charisma, which is harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner; 'it' as sex appeal dates from the 1920s It Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting remark is sharp and hurtful.

clue.text: Individual surrounded by noise is physically exhausted

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside the noise word

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A person worn out by a racket all around.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in is an informal phrase for utterly worn out.

clue.text: Greeting little children at last when they ask for a treat?

definitions.text: when they ask for a treat?

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
wee means little

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of children

explanation.surface: Welcoming small kids who come round asking for sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes N, the end of 'children'. WEE is Scottish for little.
explanation.definitionFit: On 31 October children go trick-or-treating, asking for sweets.

clue.text: Deck with gold trim

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to lop is to trim or cut off

explanation.surface: A ship's deck with gilded edging.
explanation.walkthrough: The orlop is the lowest deck of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Am I to travel in a foreign land, my friend?

definitions.text: in a foreign land, my friend

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A traveller asks a companion whether to journey abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIGO is Spanish for friend, hence 'in a foreign land'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish-speaking countries a pal is called amigo.

clue.text: Fish on black item of jewellery

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the fish word after the black one

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fish set on a dark piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bangle is a rigid bracelet worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Explosive old enemy of Israelites

definitions.meaning: a blasting explosive based on ammonium nitrate
a member of the biblical people of Ammon, foes of Israel

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a blasting compound and the biblical people of Ammon, enemies of Israel.

clue.text: Good talk by the old man shows spirit

parts.note: rap means talk, chat
pa, father, is one's old man

explanation.surface: A pleasant chat with Dad reveals his character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like character or mood but means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue.

clue.text: Steroid'-- there's no danger if it's properly administered

indicators.note: administered means dealt out, so the letters of no danger are put in order

explanation.surface: A safe hormone, given correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Androgens such as testosterone are male sex hormones, steroid compounds.
